original_record.question:
Which of the shapes cannot be split into two triangles using a single straight line?
<image1>
original_record.subject: combinatorial geometry

answer_verification.method: Any quadrilateral can be split along a diagonal into two triangles; a triangle can be split from a vertex to the opposite side. Two triangles sharing a straight cut have union boundary at most four noncollinear vertices, not six. Thus hexagon A is impossible.
